investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T04:40:28–04:41:02Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because every sibling check shares the exact same error message and no evidence was collected by any check, the failure is localized to the shared upstream swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual eval's logic or contract.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents) returned a 502 bad_gateway during the eval window, preventing agent provisioning from starting. This caused all three remote-agents checks to fail before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be collected, making every contract assertion unverifiable. The failure is an eval-observed infrastructure availability event; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-08-31T04:40–04:41Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because agent creation is the first step in every remote-agent check, the swarm gateway being unreachable caused a total upstream failure that prevented any evidence from being collected.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agent check calls POST /api/agents as its first step, which in turn proxies to the swarm ELB. The ELB returned a connection error, the production-api surfaced it as HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway", and the eval runner received no agent identity or runtime response — leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
